selection.status: All 21 raw AAI v5.0.1 frontier configurations in the supplied four-provider Standard comparison; task-fit exceptions are separate. Not a live API or account-access test.

LM.description: Candidate for trivial, tightly bounded work with inexpensive acceptance checks.

L.description: Retained Luna Max profile for explicit selection or custom pools, not a synonym for Luna Medium.

TL.description: Use for small, clearly specified code fixes, concise writing, and straightforward visual interpretation with inexpensive acceptance checks.

TM.description: Default Terra option for bounded implementation, source-grounded writing, visual interpretation, and screen-based workflows. Verify required tools and saved results.

TH.description: Use for harder diagnosis, multi-step visual reasoning, or computer-use work when additional reasoning is worth testing. Prefer it over Medium when checked quality gains justify the additional time and usage.

SL.description: Candidate for routine bounded work with clear acceptance checks.

SM.description: General-purpose implementation or independent verification candidate, depending on the active pool.

SH.description: Candidate for assignments where uncertainty or likely repair work justifies additional reasoning.

SX.description: Candidate for difficult implementation, debugging, or integration with explicit acceptance checks.

SMAX.description: Candidate for demanding implementation or independent code verification, not an automatic escalation requirement.

AL.description: Browser-specialist candidate in Codex-primary Balanced and a general candidate in Codex-burn. Verify the actual worker has required tools.

AM.description: Retained Astra Medium profile for explicit selection or custom pools.

AH.description: Browser-specialist candidate in Codex-primary Performance and a general candidate in Codex-burn. Verify required tools before dispatch.

AX.description: Retained Astra XHigh profile for explicit selection or custom pools.

AMAX.description: Candidate for demanding work or specialist verification where its tools and task fit justify the route. Independent QA/browser candidate in Amusing; verify required tools and observed behavior, not clean-code authority.

HMED.description: Candidate for small, well-scoped worker assignments with concrete checks.

HH.description: Candidate for bounded delegation when additional Haiku reasoning may reduce controller repair work.

HM.description: Bounded Haiku XHigh worker candidate, also used by the optional Opus/Haiku preset.

HK.description: Retained Haiku XHigh profile with a soft 100K context target, not an independently enforced cap.

HMAX.description: Candidate for bounded delegation where higher Haiku reasoning is worth testing against accepted-task throughput.

SNH.description: Middle-pool candidate for work needing stronger judgment than a bounded Haiku assignment.

SNX.description: Exact retained Sonnet XHigh option for economical knowledge-work comparison.

OM.description: General-purpose implementation and integration candidate in Claude-primary pools.

OH.description: General-purpose Claude-primary candidate or independent review candidate in Codex-primary Balanced. Role restrictions come from the active pool.

OX.description: General-purpose Claude-primary candidate or independent review candidate in Codex-primary Performance. Role restrictions come from the active pool.

OMAX.description: Candidate for demanding Claude-primary work or a justified Codex-primary Performance escalation.

FM.description: Selective high-capability candidate for a bounded comparison, not an automatic escalation.

FH.description: Preferred Fable candidate for difficult reasoning, specification analysis, or independent review. Verify findings against source and acceptance checks.

FX.description: Explicit trial for the hardest long-running analysis when additional reasoning is justified, not the default Fable escalation.

FMAX.description: Exceptional on-call escalation when a stronger attempt justifies additional usage, not a routine worker.

MFH.description: Investigate repository structure, existing fixes, and root causes using source evidence. Default to diagnosis and focused checks. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

MFX.description: Examine cross-system failures with competing hypotheses and challenge a proposed plan against evidence. Default to discriminating checks, not a second dispatcher. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

LL.description: Trivial extraction and mechanical edits with cheap checks.

HL.description: Cheap bounded work with explicit inputs and inexpensive checks.

EX.description: Bounded reasoning candidate when an exact Muse adapter is verified.

EMAX.description: Higher-effort Ember candidate for checked comparison.

GCM.description: General reasoning candidate with verified Gemini tools and account access.

GCH.description: General reasoning candidate with verified Gemini tools and account access.

MFMAX.description: Orchestration and steerable-prose preference trial through a verified Muse Code subscription adapter.
MFMAX.label: Muse Wonder Full

KK31.description: Terminal-engineering candidate. Choose an explicit supported runtime effort before dispatch.

GA4H.specialty: Visual reasoning and MCP tool use

DSFH.description: Budget workflow-automation experiment. Rolling alias currently maps to V4.1 Flash 1017.

GLMMAX.specialty: Writing preference and private hosting trials

MSMAX.description: Reviewed professional-document trial. Professional-reasoning evidence does not specify effort.

CYBER.description: Restricted authorized-security candidate. No runtime effort is pinned.

balanced.fit: Use for a simple one-off task with concrete inputs and an inexpensive check.
Use for bounded one-off implementation or analysis with clear ownership and acceptance criteria.
Use for a harder one-off packet that still has a narrow scope and a direct acceptance check.
Use for scoped implementation, research synthesis, or diagnosis needing judgment beyond a small Haiku packet.
Use for everyday general-purpose implementation and integration, including work spanning related files.
Use for uncertain implementation, debugging, or integration where additional reasoning is justified.

performance.fit: Use for substantive general-purpose implementation or integration with sufficiently clear requirements.

Use for demanding implementation or analysis when sustained reasoning is justified by the assignment.
Use for optional independent QA or specification review of difficult code, not authored fixes.
Start here for demanding browser or computer-use work. Confirm the actual worker's tools and session access.
Selectively escalate difficult reasoning, specification analysis, or independent review. Use a bounded worker, not authored fixes or team management.

council.fit: Develop a decision proposal, test its assumptions, and compare concrete implementation tradeoffs.
Challenge architectural choices against requirements, source evidence, and simpler alternatives.
Investigate competing hypotheses and identify evidence that distinguishes proposed approaches.
Add an optional fourth perspective on assumptions, alternatives, and decision criteria.
Advise on requirements, overlooked constraints, and alternative hypotheses without an additional vote.

codex-burn.fit: Use for a bounded authorized backlog item involving browser work, visual interpretation, or general analysis.
Use for ordinary authorized implementation or verification with a clear change surface and acceptance checks.
Use for backlog diagnosis or integration where uncertainty warrants additional reasoning.
Use for difficult authorized implementation or debugging with multiple interacting constraints.
Use for harder visual, browser, or general reasoning tasks that fit the remaining authorized backlog.
Use for demanding authorized analysis, implementation, or verification when task fit justifies sustained reasoning.

claude-burn.fit: Use for a bounded one-off backlog packet with concrete inputs, ownership, and acceptance checks.
Use for scoped authorized implementation or analysis needing more judgment than a small Haiku packet.
Use for general-purpose authorized implementation and integration spanning related files.
Use for uncertain backlog implementation or debugging where additional reasoning is justified.
Use for difficult authorized analysis, implementation, or integration with interacting requirements.
Use for demanding authorized work when sustained reasoning fits the backlog, not merely to consume allowance.

amusing.fit: Implement bounded changes in the repository's existing idioms. Prefer the smallest complete change and inexpensive acceptance checks.
Debug difficult invariants or integrate changes with interacting constraints. Require evidence that the fix addresses the cause without expanding scope.
Prefer for substantial scoped implementation or refactoring when the task fits Opus Medium. Medium is not a universal optimum, so compare the actual candidate and checks.
Independently review maintainability and architecture against the repository's existing design. Propose concrete simpler alternatives where they preserve the required behavior.
Perform demanding functional or adversarial verification with checked tool access. Report observed behavior and failures without treating this route as clean-code authority.
Selectively review conformance to explicit requirements and acceptance criteria. Cite mismatches and omissions without implementing fixes or requiring this reviewer for every change.
Investigate repository structure, existing fixes, and root causes using source evidence. Default to diagnosis and focused checks. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

Examine cross-system failures with competing hypotheses and challenge a proposed plan against evidence. Default to discriminating checks, not a second dispatcher. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

reviewer.prompt: Review the assigned work and return evidence and uncertainties. Honor the requested role, authorized checks, file ownership, and any shared deadline. Available tools do not authorize unrelated edits.

muse:muse_code_subscription.verification_scope: Existing Muse Code adapter route only. Current account access, model entitlement, tools, and effective effort require dispatch preflight.
